ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled U, and the horizontal axis is labeled I; resistor A corresponds to a curved rising volt-ampere characteristic curve, and resistor B corresponds to a straight line starting from the origin. Curve A and straight line B intersect at the same point, and in the figure horizontal dashed lines and vertical dashed lines are used to mark that the voltage corresponding to this intersection point is U1, and the current is I1. Reasoning: At a certain point on the volt-ampere characteristic curve, the resistance can be obtained from R=U/I. At the intersection point, A and B correspond to the same voltage U1 and the same current I1, so RA=U1/I1, RB=U1/I1, therefore RA=RB.
